issues.description: The release has ten Stata preparation/helper programs, the datasheet, appendix, and Company_Identifiers.xlsx, but no raw inputs or prepared regression datasets. The workbook is an identifier/name list, not an analysis panel. The 33 input requirements distinguish the actual products/tables used in all six branches; their exact field, key, producer, history, and access routes remain unresolved where not probed.

The driver calls 4_data_hist_bidding.do before 5_data_licensing.do, but licensing produces participant_EPD_clean.dta and mainHC_type.dta consumed by bidding. Reorder the existing calls so licensing completes first, retaining all six branches.

The driver leaves main_dir blank and derives raw_data, clean_data and final_data from it; helper calls in payment and segment scripts use a separate code global that is not set in supplied code. Configure project/output roots and code directory in a working copy before attempting the six branches.

The segment loop does not map an operating-income field, but the later reshape declares segment_oic. A self-written Stata fixture confirms that the absent stub does not halt reshape and yields an all-missing variable. Although the local Worldscope product labels item19602 as operating income, the author input and intended output semantics are unverified; a mapping would also change the later duplicate-drop key. Clarify author intent before any source or input change; this is not a mandatory raw-column requirement.

The single consumed author CSV is expected to contain segment fields plus company/name, nation, region and fiscal-year-end columns. The local WRDS_WS_SEGMENTS candidate confirms the item196 fields but lacks several company fields; WRDS_WS_COMPANY is a potential supplement, but the join key, uniqueness and author-compatible CSV constructor are not provided. Use the single author CSV if available; keep any raw-table merge conditional until its contract is supported.

The segment program imports NA/global NAICS text files to create clean_data crosswalks, but later reads separate gvkey_to_naics_north_america.dta and gvkey_to_naics_global.dta from raw_data. No supplied producer creates those raw-directory names; the generated files have different paths and key checks do not establish uniqueness on every later merge key (CUSIP, SEDOL, ISIN). Confirm the intended prepared files or validate a supported working-copy path/schema alignment.

The parent quarterly branch expects author-named Compustat/security DTA inputs with exact NAICS and company/location fields, merges security by gvkey/datadate, and builds lagged/differenced controls before its 2010Q1-2017Q4 output filter. The code drops its internally indexed Q4 2009 observation, but this does not establish complete pre-sample history for all controls. Local quarterly candidates cover many date/financial fields but not the full author schema (including exact naics/conm), and no producer/merge constructor is supplied.

5_data_licensing.do saves oil_block_participant.dta to clean_data, then reads the same basename from raw_data to classify hydrocarbon type. These different directories do not establish a producer-consumer handoff. Align the consumer to the produced clean_data path in a working copy.

The bidding branch comments out both post_EPD derivation statements but later labels post_EPD. The initial raw bid table is projected to a saved keep list that excludes the field. A later full epd_masterfile merge by company_standardized could add a same-named field, but the all_bidders projection also omits it, so pass-through to the final dataset is not established. Confirm the intended field source, survival path and definition before execution; do not remove the label or invent the indicator.

The productivity program requires production_field_block_EPD.dta, containing field-to-block identity, reporting flags and entity attributes, but no supplied program produces it. It is a separate prepared mapping input and cannot be inferred from the raw monthly Enverus production file alone.

actions.description: Locate compatible prepared payment, enrichment, Compustat, currency and shaming inputs for the payment branch; use documented manual/vendor source leads only after checking the exact prepared-input route.
steps: Check for the named author-prepared EITI payment workbook and each required enrichment sheet separately (`all`, `all_update`, `parent_gvkeys`); confirm their company/country or parent-country/GVKEY join keys and report-year coverage.

Check the separate Compustat North America and Global annual inputs for exact naics, issuer/date/fiscal-year keys, and the source history required by the coded lagged capex fractions. At t-5 the ratio reaches capx_(t-5)/assets_(t-6), subject to consecutive-fiscal-year checks; preserve missingness and do not infer an input lower bound. Local annual candidates expose naicsh, so establish an author-consistent mapping before using them.

Stage and verify the payment-specific country/currency/year/unit FX sheet and the monthly Compustat exchange product under both consumed filenames; verify the merge key and rates for all matched periods.

Locate the 2013 CPI workbook sheet, EPD masterfile, English Factiva firm-year coverage and the two distinct activist files. Datasheet provenance is a lead; it does not establish current rows, routes, or entitlement.
Keep manual EITI/EPD/activist sources and Factiva as separate products; do not reconstruct author-prepared tables unless the necessary source definitions and mappings are confirmed.
validation: Verify required columns, date ranges, country/company keys and expected merge uniqueness for each input before a future driver attempt.

Confirm payment observations from 2010 onward and the code’s consecutive-fiscal-year conditions for lagged capex fractions; preserve row-level missingness and do not require all lags to be nonmissing or infer a source lower bound. Confirm FX keys and CPI 2013 mappings.
Confirm the shaming helper inputs have `gvkey`, year and campaign/media fields matching the payment branch.

If using the local Worldscope catalog candidates instead, verify issuer-year joins and company-field uniqueness between WRDS_WS_SEGMENTS and any company-information supplement before constructing the author CSV; the join and constructor are currently unsupported.

Locate the author-prepared Worldscope parent fundamentals DTA or document how the local annual candidate maps to ws_id, year, assets, ROA, local assets and liabilities; retain the presample history required by the coded lagged controls, with exact lower bound and row-level missingness unverified.
Locate annual exchange rates and all three CPI workbooks (1998-2015, 2016, 2017), plus EPD/media/activist-investment inputs; verify country codes, units and periods before merging.
validation: Confirm source has all ten segment field sets and exact firm/year keys; keep the segment_oic behavior as a separate author-intent question; do not add item19602 as a required input column.
Verify CPI 1998-2017 rows and FX country-year units; check parent lag construction through 2017.
Confirm both pre-2014 and 2014+ segment observations remain available for the coded regression sample.

review_notes: Assessed target is the ten supplied Stata files implementing six regression-data preparation outputs plus one prepared field-production intermediate. Datasheet and appendix describe further estimation/event-study work; no corresponding estimator/event-study program is supplied in this package, so these analyses are contextual and not added as mandatory scope.
Company_Identifiers.xlsx is a readable one-row-sampled identifier workbook with six analysis-labeled sheets; it is not a prepared panel or an alternative route for any of the empirical inputs.

The local SAS observations are exact product candidates and bounded one-row evidence only. Field matches do not establish full-history, key uniqueness, author schema construction or complete availability.

Datasheet notes EITI, EPD, TI CPI and activist information as public/manual collection leads; Factiva and Enverus as commercial product provenance. No public source was live-verified in this assigned check. No catalog hit/miss is treated as proof of access or license status.

The licensing program leaves version empty. The provided synthetic Stata fixture shows `isid participant country year` succeeds via default/on abbreviation to the retained participantintname key; explicit ID mode fails because collapse does not retain participantID. No macro edit is proposed; future setup should confirm varabbrev on and check the full key.

The segment reshape can execute with all-missing segment_oic; catalog item19602 is a possible operating-income source, but author intent and duplicate-removal effects are unverified. No raw OIC field or source edit is mandatory until clarified.

For bidding post_EPD, the raw-workbook keep list omits the field; the full EPD merge could supply it, but its later all_bidders projection also omits it. The final field source/pass-through and derivation remain unresolved.

Annual payment lag5 is the capex fraction at t-5 with denominator assets at t-6, subject to consecutive-year checks. Code preserves missingness and does not state the intended lower source bound. The parent quarterly filter/drop similarly does not prove a single preceding quarter makes every lag available.
The work item allowed exact SAS catalog probes and bounded approved checks. No author program or study dataset was run; no source file was edited; execution_verified remains false.
